reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes sending BNB to and activating a front-running contract that allegedly trades tokens and returns 90% of stated profits to the viewer, while claiming earnings of several hundred BNB and possible returns of up to 1000 BNB per day. The sampled BscScan frame shows a zero balance and no matching entries, providing material counterevidence to the claimed success, although it does not establish the contract's actual behavior or outcome.

follow the description of the video as far as downloading MetaMask and also. Funding it, make sure that it's connected to the Binance Smart Chain
the next step in this process is just funding your contract
For the sake of this video, 0.2 BNB. Might as well make it a 0.4, a little bit extra, sometimes helps.
The action button then engages all the constructors that I built in as far as engaging the Pancake Router.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present every outcome as certain. He says returns arrive "generally," that waiting "usually" takes a few minutes, and that larger earnings are something viewers "could" have, not something they will have. He also limits where the contract is supposed to work. Those qualifications do not prove the bot works, but they matter when assessing whether this is a guaranteed-return pitch rather than a technically specific, if optimistic, account of an experiment.

citations.quote: We usually only need a wait a few. Minutes before we get a deposit back into our address.
You know you could have upwards of 1000 BNB a day. If you use a larger amount than I started with.
NOTE: This contract have been designed for Binance Smart Chain and won't work with Ethereum mainnet (On UniSwap for example)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The funding and activation steps in the opening are real, but neither step by itself establishes deceptive solicitation. The cited BscScan view is a snapshot with a zero balance and no matching entries; it does not establish what the contract subsequently did. The speaker's prospective earnings language is conditional, so the opening should not treat its largest figure as a promised payout.

citations.quote: You know you could have upwards of 1000 BNB a day. If you use a larger amount than I started with.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Qualifiers do not change the core pitch. The speaker instructs viewers to fund the contract, says it will send 90% of profits back to their wallets, and claims an extraordinary result during the demonstration. The cited snapshot cannot establish the contract's eventual outcome, but it also supplies no corroboration for the claimed returns.

from there it will take 90% will automatically trans back to your wallet.
Yeah, it's. Already around 50x.

opening.argument: Judge, the central activity is a walkthrough of a Solidity workflow: the speaker creates a contract file, selects a compiler version, compiles, and deploys through an injected wallet. The sampled screens show the Remix editor and deployment controls. The discussion of funding occurs within that operational sequence. A tutorial can describe a claimed use case without independently proving its performance; the appropriate reading is a technical demonstration whose earnings claims remain unverified, not a stand-alone request to send funds to the speaker.

citations.quote: Under Contracts, I'm going to create a new contract, which is with this new file. Create new file icon on the top left.
So we go to version 6.6, solidity, and that's it. Let me go compile frontrunbot. There we go, it compiled.
We're going to deploy this to our wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening accurately identifies instructions to fund and activate the contract, but those steps also fit the demonstrated deploy-and-test workflow. It cites no observed transfer to the speaker. The zero-balance BscScan frame raises a fair question about the claimed results, yet a single displayed account view does not establish the contract's behavior after activation.

citations.quote: So we're going to send some funds to that contract that we just created.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not merely about compiling Solidity. Its instructions culminate in funding a contract and pressing an action button that the speaker says will trade automatically and return profits. He urges viewers toward the procedure while reporting a roughly 50-fold result. Showing editor controls does not verify the trading mechanism or neutralize the funded-return pitch.

The action button then engages all the constructors that I built in as far as engaging the Pancake Router. Router. It automatically buys and sells for you.
from there it will take 90% will automatically trans back to your wallet.
Yeah, it's. Already around 50x.

opening.argument: Judge, the described transaction is framed as funding a contract the viewer has just created, using the viewer's wallet and ordinary named development tools. The supplied instructions do not ask the viewer to disclose a seed phrase, pay the speaker, or recruit anyone. Funding a contract is consequential, but a deposit alone does not show where its funds ultimately go or whether its code performs as advertised. The strongest supported concern is that the proposed trading returns are unverified, not that the record demonstrates diversion to an identified recipient.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening establishes a funded-return claim, but it does not trace the deposited BNB through the contract or identify a recipient of diverted funds. Its BscScan snapshot shows no matching entries, which challenges the success story without resolving the contract's actual operation. A careful judge should distinguish an unsupported earnings claim from proof of a particular theft mechanism.

citations.quote: So we're going to send some funds to that contract that we just created.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a shown seed-phrase request or traced theft does not make this ordinary commerce. The speaker supplies contract code, tells viewers to fund the deployed contract, and promises automated trading with most profits returned to their wallets. The sampled account view does not establish the contract's outcome, but it offers no independent support for those earnings claims either.
